applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 1 (northwest area near Building 1, north of main entrance)
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 1 located only 1.1 feet from adjacent concrete sidewalk (requires 2-foot minimum per code). Transformer Pad 3 (Building 8) located only 0.5 feet from adjacent sidewalk or walkway (requires 2-foot minimum). Both pads violate minimum sidewalk setback requirement.

No documentation of Austin Energy Design written approval for any clearance reductions is visible in the submitted plans. If any transformer pads are proposed with clearances less than 5 feet to buildings, written approval confirming compliance with all exception conditions (not in confined space, 10+ ft to windows/doors/ducts, 15+ ft vertical clearance, 3-hour fire rating) must be provided.

Transformer pad hot-stick use area (access door side) dimensions and clearance zones not shown or dimensioned on electrical plan. Without specific designation of the hot-stick use area on each pad and dimension callouts showing 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure, compliance with minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified.

No cross-section drawings are provided showing vertical clearances in access paths to transformer pads. Grading plan is plan view only. Cross-sections demonstrating minimum vertical clearances from overhead structures, parking garage overhangs, or enclosed building areas must be provided if such features are present above transformer pad access routes.

Equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on electrical or equipment schedules. Drainage direction around transformer pad locations is not explicitly shown on grading plan. For oil-filled equipment, liquid must flow away from building. Drainage direction callouts and equipment type specification are required for compliance verification.

While transformer pads appear to be located within the site boundary on the electrical plan, no explicit dimension callouts or notes confirm that all 5 transformer pads are 100% on private property rather than straddling property lines or located in public right-of-way. Dimension callouts from pads to property boundary lines must be provided.

Transformer pads are shown on electrical plan (Sheet 21) but not overlaid on grading plan (Sheet 11) which shows easement locations. Cannot verify that transformer pads are not located in drainage easements, water easements, sewer easements, or electrical easements under overhead lines. Plans must clearly show transformer pad locations in relation to all easements with notation confirming no conflicts or noting required Austin Energy Design written approvals.

No transformer easements are explicitly shown, labeled, or dimensioned on the site plan, plat, or easement exhibit sheets. General electric easements are noted on the grading plan, but specific transformer pad easements (width and location determined by Austin Energy Design for accessibility) are not delineated. Transformer easement boundaries must be shown with widths specified.

Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters is shown on the electrical plan but the routing path is not explicitly called out or dimensioned to confirm 100% routing on private property. No notes or dimension callouts state that the entire electrical service line from transformer to meter remains on private property and does not cross public right-of-way or easements.

No transformer pad detail sheets from Austin Energy Design are provided showing approved pad dimensions for the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase). The electrical design plan does not specify service type or reference AE Design detail sheets. Pad dimensions and specifications must match AE Design-approved standards obtained from Austin Energy Design.

applicableAreas: Areas near transformer pads with proposed trees (Buildings 1, 8, 6-7)
findings.comment: Trees are proposed on the landscape plan in areas where transformer pads are located (near Buildings 1, 8, and 6-7). However, trees are not dimensioned in relation to transformer pad locations on either the landscape plan or electrical plan. Tree species cross-reference to ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) column is not provided, making verification of utility compatibility impossible for trees within 10 lateral feet of equipment or 15 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors.

applicableAreas: Landscape areas adjacent to transformer pads
findings.comment: Landscape plan shows proposed shrubs and vegetation but does not show transformer pad locations. Therefore, clearance distances from transformer access door sides (10 lateral feet required) and from other sides (5 lateral feet required) cannot be verified. Landscape plan must explicitly show transformer pad locations with callouts indicating shrub/vegetation clearance zones.

applicableAreas: Trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electrical equipment
findings.comment: Landscape plan does not show transformer pad locations, and no root barrier details are provided. If trees are proposed within 20 lateral feet of transformer pads, root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from equipment) must be detailed and shown on landscape plan. Cannot verify compliance without transformer pad overlay and root barrier specifications.

Although measurements from transformer pads to identified utility lines (water, wastewater, storm drain) show clearances well in excess of 12 inches (40-78 feet), the plans do not explicitly dimension all 12-inch minimum clearances from transformer pads to other underground utilities (reclaimed water, communications, gas, fuel, steam). Specific dimension callouts confirming 12-inch minimum horizontal and vertical clearances from all other underground utilities must be provided.

Plans do not include explicit dimension callouts or notes confirming that transformer pads and Austin Energy underground facilities are not located over or under other utility lines, and that customer buildings/foundations/structures are not installed over Austin Energy underground facilities. Cross-utility coordination notes or dimension callouts confirming no conflicts must be provided.

If overhead distribution lines are present on the site, minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead distribution line conductors (primary, neutral, secondary extending from ground to sky) must be verified. Overhead line locations and transformer pad locations are not overlaid on site plan with dimension callouts. If overhead distribution exists, clearance callouts must be provided.

If overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors exist on the site, minimum 15-foot radius clearance measured from the conductor centerline must be shown. Overhead conductor locations relative to transformer pad locations are not dimensioned on the utility or site plan. If overhead distribution exists, 15-foot radius clearance zone callouts must be provided.
